harper: hey team, harper here (first week). trying to build the inference runtime from source on WSL2 (Ubuntu 22.04) with an RTX 4090 loaner. followed the onboarding doc but hit multiple CUDA / nvcc errors. anyone available to sanity-check? :wave:

zoe: welcome! can you paste the top cmake/make error and `nvcc --version` + `nvidia-smi`? WSL2 GPU passthrough can be tricky.

harper: sure. nvcc -> "Cuda compilation tools, release 12.2, V12.2.89". nvidia-smi shows Driver 535, CUDA 12.2. main errors during cmake/make:

```
/opt/cuda/include/host_config.h:56:10: fatal error: cuda_runtime_api.h: No such file or directory
 #include <cuda_runtime_api.h>
ld: cannot find -lcuda
nvcc: error: unsupported GNU version! gcc versions later than 11 are not supported by this release.
```

devex: a few quick checks: 1) make sure CUDA toolkit (not just driver) is installed under /usr/local/cuda-12.2 and CUDA_HOME set. 2) WSL exposes libcuda under /usr/lib/wsl which sometimes confuses the linker. 3) nvcc gcc compatibility: install gcc-11/g++-11 or use our dev-container image.

zoe: run these commands and paste output: `ls -l /usr/local/cuda-12.2/include`, `ls -l /usr/lib/wsl/libcuda.so*`, `echo $CUDA_HOME $LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `gcc --version`. If /opt/cuda exists from an old install remove or fix the symlink.

harper: ran checks: /usr/local/cuda-12.2 exists and include has headers, but /opt/cuda is symlinked to an old non-existent path. libcuda only exists at /usr/lib/wsl/libcuda.so -> /proc/driver/nvidia/000. CUDA_HOME was empty. exported vars and re-ran cmake; now cmake finds CUDA but linker still fails with -lcuda.

devex: if libcuda is only available under /usr/lib/wsl, add that to link dirs or prefer building in a full VM/container. recommended: use `ghcr.io/redwood-inference/dev-container:cuda-12.2` or request an infra VM. Also run `sudo ldconfig` after installing toolkit or add `/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64` to `/etc/ld.so.conf.d/cuda.conf`.

infra: I can provision a 48h gpu-dev VM with matching cuda/gcc if you want — reply "infra vm" and i'll create it. We do that for new hires often.

harper: i'll take the VM, thanks. one more quick Q: the build doc mentions `gcc-11` specifically. is switching required?

zoe: nvcc complains for host compilers newer than supported by that CUDA version. use gcc-11 or the container toolchain. CMake flags: `-DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=/usr/bin/gcc-11 -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=/usr/bin/g++-11 -DCUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR=/usr/local/cuda-12.2`.

harper: infra ticket opened (DEVVM-721). switching to VM and dev-container for now. will update this thread after I try. thanks all! :tada:
